The with-gauge model with rain to midnight has fewer false warnings among its onset warnings than with NLDAS rain (56% against 63%) at the same hits.

With the river gauge nothing changes at lead 2 and 3 (NSE gap closed 2% and -1%, onset gap 4% and 3%), as expected for rain that has not fallen yet. Without the gauge the rain of day t also helps a little at lead 2 (onsets 12.0% against control 9.5%, every training above every control training; NSE 0.332 against 0.286), since there the flow state is not given; the same size as NLDAS rain.
verdict: The code, the numbers, the clock and the saved networks of E1 hold up under independent recomputation; I found no leakage and no arithmetic error. Every headline number of results/rain_to_midnight.json was reproduced with my own code (0.0 deviation against the engine; my own pooled onset counts give 183 of 611 for rain to midnight and 114 of 611 for the rain table alone); the three-seed files are exact means of their seeds; my independently rebuilt daily series (summer time by zoneinfo and by a hand-written rule, equal at all 298296 hours) reproduces the stored forecasts of all 12 saved networks bit for bit; no hour after local midnight of day t enters day t, also when tested through the saved networks; scalers, thresholds and early stopping use the training and validation years only; the figure shows the JSON's numbers to within a pixel; flood.py is byte-identical to the hand-in copy and test_flood.py passes. What the experiment shows is smaller than its sentence suggests. Rain up to midnight lifts the share of onsets warned 1 day ahead from 19% to 30% (control 21%, verdict NOT YET), but the NLDAS evening rain gave exactly the same 183 hits, one of the three trainings is at 27.5%, and the control is not flat, so the work order's success criterion (clearly above 30% in every seed, control flat) is NOT met with the river gauge; without the gauge the three trainings are above 30% and the control is flat, but NLDAS already scores 31.6% there, so the extra hours add nothing the evening rain had not. The outcome sentence is fair arithmetic but must not be quoted without those facts. About 8.5 of the 11 points come from the rain of day t itself and about 3 from having a second rain product. One premise rests on documentation rather than proof, that Open-Meteo stamps the END of the hour; the data lean the same way and flipping it would change the result by at most 1.3 points. Open before E1 can enter the report: the ridge/random-forest yardstick, the resampling ranges and a matched-window control.

round_2.verdict: The extension holds up under independent recomputation; I found no leakage, no wrong number and no broken control. Every number I recomputed from results/preds equals the results file: the headline scores of the three new sets and the two simple models (hits 125, 133, 194, 164 and 165 of 611, as stated), 273 engine values, the readings, gain-rule, closure, yardstick and verdict fields (more than 2,000 numbers, flags and words, 0 differences) and the by_period table. The two new windows are proved with my own code: rain_to_09 ends 15 h before the issue time, the UTC-day window 4 to 6 h before it, and nothing after a window's end enters its value (56 perturbation cases); my independent series, and the NLDAS column rebuilt as 10_rain_timing.py builds it, reproduce all nine new networks and the twelve old ones bit for bit (max difference 0.0), and the NLDAS day is the UTC day to within an hour by my own estimate (at least 4 h before the issue time). The simple models are built as the recipe says (the new series enters as the same ten rain features as the Daymet rain, causal, 33 features), refit by the stored settings they reproduce the stored forecasts (ridge exactly, 0.0, when the rain is summed the script's way; forest to 7e-15, the order of the parallel sum over the trees), and no data after 2000-09-30 enters a fit. The date and attribution of the ERA5 assimilation change (17 July 2009, Beck et al. 2019, footnote 5) are verifiable on the paper's page, so the wording needs no 'unverified' mark; ECMWF's own page confirms the hour-ending convention and that rain comes only from the 06/18 UTC forecasts. The figure matches the JSON (30 markers within 0.16 points / 0.0015 NSE), --rescore reproduces JSON and figure, --extend with nothing to train trains and writes nothing, flood.py, features.py and 02_baselines.py are byte-identical to the hand-in zip. What the new results mean: the matched-window control is flat (20.5% against 18.7%), so the +9.5 points of onsets (183 against 125 hits, every training above) are the worth of the hours after about 09:00; in ERA5 the evening hours beyond the UTC day add +8.2 but NLDAS, whose day ends at about the UTC-day hour, reaches the same 30%, so product quality matters as much as hours; both products together 31.8% (194), not clearly more; the simple models given the same input warn of 26.8% and 27.0% (in onsets the new input helps ridge more than the LSTM), equal on NSE and on the validated warning level, about 3 points behind the LSTM on onsets at the plain level (paired p about 0.04); the E1 success rule is still not met. One thing must change before documents are rebuilt: outcome_full, which documents quote verbatim, still carries only the 'control is not flat' caveat; it must also say that the matched control is flat and that simple models get the same gain, or readers will take the gain for an artefact. The rest is should-fix: pair the readings, add the onset comparison for the yardstick, record the script hash per pass, and keep the review scripts in the project. three_to_five_seed_changes.outcome_full_three_seeds: Given the rain of the whole issue day up to local midnight (hourly ERA5 rain from 00:00 to 24:00 by the local wall clock) as one extra input to the LSTM with the river gauge, onsets warned 1 day ahead go from 19% to 30% (control 21%); the verdict is NOT YET. The NLDAS rain up to the evening gives the same share (30%, 183 hits of 611 in both); the three single trainings with the rain to midnight span 27.5% to 31.6%; the control is not flat (21% against 19% with the rain table alone); the success rule of the work order (clearly above the NLDAS result in every training, control flat) is not met. The control with the same rain over the table's own window is flat (20.5% against 18.7% with the rain table alone), so the gain of 9.5 points comes from the hours after about 09:00 (75 onsets warned only by the rain to midnight against 17 only by that control). Ridge regression and the random forest given the same input warn of 26.8% and 27.0% (the new input adds 16.2 and 8.8 points to them, 11.3 to the LSTM), so the gain does not need the network.
